questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “CSS Performance Fundamentals”?
questions.explanation: The source curriculum lists “Understanding rendering work” under “CSS Performance Fundamentals”. The lesson applies this syllabus point to a small CSS example and a browser check.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports reliable work with css performance fundamentals?
options: Reproduce the issue, inspect computed styles, change one variable, then retest the original scenario.
Add !important to every declaration so conflicts disappear.
Assume the newest CSS feature behaves identically in all browsers.
Remove focus styles because a mouse user can see the hovered element.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the issue, inspect computed styles, change one variable, then retest the original scenario.
questions.explanation: The key practice is: Reproduce the issue, inspect computed styles, change one variable, then retest the original scenario. For advanced features, inspect the relevant documentation and target-browser compatibility.

questions.prompt: If an example related to “CSS Performance Fundamentals” does not look or behave as expected, what is the strongest first response?
options: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
Add several unrelated overrides until the screenshot looks closer.
Only check the default viewport and skip interactive states.
Treat an unused declaration as proof that the browser is broken.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
questions.explanation: A repeatable inspection loop is more reliable than layering on overrides: inspect what matched, identify the computed value, change one cause, and retest.
